title: Threat Detection Library - Cisco SD-WAN Privileged Admin Action Validation Entry
description: Schema for a single entry in data/cisco-sdwan-privileged-admin-validations.json -- this library's third validation catalogue, alongside the RHEL and FortiGate ones. Not a production detection rule: its 'search' field is a one-shot presence check ('did the expected event show up'), and its distinguishing fields (safe_test, test_step, rollback_step, test_result) describe executing an action once against a controlled Cisco SD-WAN Manager/WAN Edge deployment and confirming the telemetry/detection fired. See docs/validations.md for the full rationale.

id.description: Stable catalogue identifier, sourced from the original workbook's Event ID column.

platform.description: Platform(s) this validation applies to. Every entry in this catalogue is Cisco SD-WAN-scoped today -- Cisco SD-WAN Manager (formerly vManage) and WAN Edge devices; exact UI/API names vary by software release, per the source workbook's own notes.

category.description: Original test grouping, e.g. Administrator, Device Template, Centralized Policy.

event_type.description: High-level privileged activity taxonomy, e.g. Administrator management, Policy management, Routing configuration.

title.description: Canonical description of the privileged action.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of the action (the workbook's Examples column).

typical_mechanism.description: Common SD-WAN Manager GUI path or REST API mechanism.

privilege_level.description: Expected privilege context, e.g. Manager administrator / RBAC-controlled.

mitre_attack.description: Resolved against the live MITRE ATT&CK STIX corpus at conversion time -- not copied verbatim from the workbook's ATT&CK Tactic column, which still used the pre-split 'Defense Evasion' tactic name, and not from its ATT&CK Technique column, two of whose values were revoked/renumbered technique IDs (T1562.001, T1562.004) redirected via MITRE's own revoked-by relationship. A minority of entries (those with no technique to anchor a lookup, or a free-text guess with no real technique ID) may have an empty tactics/techniques array rather than a guessed mapping.

note.description: Optional context note from the source workbook, e.g. 'context dependent' or a MITRE renumbering redirect.

primary_telemetry.description: Primary Cisco SD-WAN telemetry expected to record the action.

safe_test.description: Whether this action is suitable for controlled testing without intentional disruptive impact.

test_step.description: Command or action used to generate the event.

test_result.description: Pass/Fail/Partial/Not Tested tracking field -- set by whoever actually runs the validation, not by this library.

sdwan_manager_context.description: The SD-WAN Manager GUI area/context the action is performed under, e.g. 'Administration / Users'.

expected_object_config_path.description: Expected SD-WAN Manager object/configuration path touched by the action.

expected_telemetry_type.description: Expected telemetry category, e.g. 'Manager audit log; authentication/API access logs'.

expected_source_ip.description: Expected management client/API source IP where available.

expected_device_identity.description: Expected Manager/controller hostname or WAN Edge system-ip/device UUID.

expected_command_change.description: Expected command/configuration change recorded in telemetry.

expected_fields.description: Minimum fields useful for validation and detection.

validation_spl.description: Starter SPL to validate event presence in Splunk -- a presence check, not a tuned detection rule.
